Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

- Agreed performance targets (initial ask): p95 latency <= 120ms for streaming responses on typical prompts (~120–150 tokens).
- Tail requirement: 99th <= 250ms (you mentioned this is important for user-facing flows).
- Throughput: target sustained throughput of ~300 qps for peak flows, with the ability to handle ~50 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: must support token-by-token streaming with low head-start latency and continued KV/cache warmness for repeated user sessions.

Action items we committed to:
1) Redwood to share a draft benchmark methodology (prompt sets, harness, measurement definitions) for your review — aim to make runs reproducible across our infra.
2) EdgeFin to share representative prompt sets and any special long-tail prompts (or we can synthesize a matching distribution).
3) Schedule a 60m benchmarking sync next week to walk through the harness and run an initial smoke test.

I've attached the call notes and the recording for reference. We'll include Rishi and Dylan from our side on the benchmarking details.

Does the above look right? If so, I'll push the draft methodology by tomorrow EOD and propose times for the sync.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications / must-haves from our side before we finalize the methodology:

- Latency details: the 120ms p95 target is for streaming token delivery (i.e., time from model emitting first token to token arrival at client). For full-response latency we care about p95 ~ 200ms on average prompt lengths, but streaming p95 <= 120ms is the primary SLO.
- Tail: we also need p99 <= 250ms for interactive sessions.
- Throughput / concurrency: 300 qps sustained across the service during peak 10-min windows, with support for 50 concurrent websocket streaming sessions.
- Warm vs cold: warm instances with KV/cache warmed will be the main operating mode; we need to understand warm-start behavior and steady-state latencies. Cold-starts can be higher but should be documented.
- Reproducibility: please include RNG/seed control, deterministic tokenization details, and a way for us to reproduce runs (dockerized harness or fixed container).

Also attached a small set of representative prompts and a couple of long-tail examples (edgefin_prompts_examples.json).

We're happy to review your draft methodology and then run a joint smoke test. Prefer Wed or Thu next week for the sync.

Best,

Mike Turner

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EdgeFin performance SLO / benchmark methodology — follow-up

Thanks — quick methodology summary and next steps. I put a short checklist below and attached the initial harness bundle.

Methodology highlights (draft):
- Prompt sets: use EdgeFin-provided prompts + synthetic distribution matching token-length histogram; include a separate "long-tail" file for 0.5% heavy prompts. Prompts will be manifest-ed in JSONL with metadata (approx_token_count, intent_tag).
- Tokenization: fixed tokenizer version + pre-tokenization script included in harness; we will record token counts per prompt in results to ensure apples-to-apples comparison.
- Latency definitions:
  - Streaming head-start latency: time from request start to first token arrival at client (measured at client-side stub).
  - Per-token latency: median time between successive tokens during streaming (for throughput analysis).
  - Full-response latency: time from request start to final token arrival.
  - p50/p95/p99 measured across provided distribution and across a sliding 10-minute peak window.
- Throughput: reported as completed requests/sec and successful streamed sessions/sec over 10-minute windows.
- Concurrency: harness supports N concurrent websocket clients (we'll default to 50), each sending sequential prompts according to a per-session think-time distribution.
- Warmup: recommended 5-minute warmup run before measurement windows; we will capture warmup vs steady-state metrics.
- Reproducibility: harness runs in docker; we pin runtime, tokenizer, model-version. RNG seeds configurable; we log seed values and the full prompt manifest and harness configuration.
- Failure modes and retries: define success criteria (no dropped streams, token correctness thresholds) and report error rates; include end-to-end logs and server-side traces if available.

Deliverables (next 48 hours):
1) Repo link + docker image: https://git.redwood.com/benchmarks/edgefin-harness
2) Benchmark spec doc in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/edgefin/benchmark-spec (I updated the draft)
3) Initial smoke-run plan and a checklist for the joint session.

Attachment: benchmark_harness_v1.tar.gz (stub) — contains scripts, dockerfile, sample manifests.

I'll coordinate with Dylan to have the smoke test scripts ready for Wed morning. Mike — let us know which time works best for you.
